items.quote: The Slack Web API is an interface for querying information from and enacting change in a Slack workspace.
items.why: Describes Web API as interface; no messaging, channels or DMs mentioned.

items.quote: Slack apps are installed with a v2 OAuth 2.0 flow.
items.why: Shows OAuth 2.0 install flow only; no bot/user tokens, PKCE, or other methods.

items.quote: User tokens allow you to work directly on behalf of users when necessary.
items.why: Confirms user tokens exist; says nothing about bearer_token category or xoxb/xoxp details.

items.quote: OAuth allows a user in any Slack workspace to install your app.
items.why: Confirms any workspace user can install via OAuth; no free-creation or self-serve gate.

items.quote: Only apps published in the Slack Marketplace and internal apps can use MCP at this time; unlisted apps are prohibited from using MCP.
items.why: Says Marketplace/internal apps only for MCP; no free-tier or Web API claim.

items.quote: The Web API is a collection of HTTP RPC-style methods , all with URLs in the form https://slack.com/api/METHOD_FAMILY.method .
items.why: States Web API is HTTP RPC-style; nothing on websocket, Socket Mode or breadth.

items.quote: With the Slack MCP server, your integrated apps can search channels, send messages, and perform other Slack actions through MCP clients.
items.why: Shows Slack MCP server exists; URL and vendor-official status not in quote.

items.quote: Workspace admins can approve and manage all MCP client integrations, keeping your Slack data safe.
items.why: Admin approval of MCP integrations; says nothing about verdict or build_now blocker.
